## Introduction

A **MAC (Media Access Control) address** is the 48-bit hardware identifier of a
network interface, usually written as six hexadecimal bytes such as
`00:00:5E:00:53:2A`. The first bytes identify the manufacturer: they are a
block assigned by the [IEEE Registration
Authority](https://regauth.standards.ieee.org/standards-ra-web/pub/view.html#registries).

`MAC.address` is an R package to work with these addresses: list the ones of
your own device and of your local network, extract them from text, validate
and normalize them, and find out who made the device. Version **0.1.0** is now
available on **CRAN**, and it depends only on base R.

👉 https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=MAC.address

---

## Installation

Requires **R ≥ 4.0.0**.

```r
# From CRAN
install.packages("MAC.address")

# Development version, from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("EnriquePH/mac-address")

library(MAC.address)
```

---

## Examples

### Addresses of this device and its network

`get_MAC()` returns the MAC addresses of the local network interfaces, named by
interface, on Linux, macOS and Windows:

```r
get_MAC()
#>            enp3s0f1              wlp2s0
#> "9C:5C:8E:12:34:56" "10:02:B5:AB:CD:EF"
```

`get_arp_table()` reads the ARP cache: the IP and MAC addresses of the
neighbors your computer has talked to. Combined with `lookup_vendor()` it tells
you what kind of devices are on the network:

```r
arp <- get_arp_table()
arp$vendor <- lookup_vendor(arp$mac)
arp
#>            ip               mac interface        vendor
#> 1 192.168.1.1 D4:61:95:00:11:22    wlp2s0 zte corporation
```

Both functions only read the local network configuration; they do not send any
packets.

### Search, validate and normalize

`search_MAC()` extracts addresses from free text in colon, hyphen and Cisco
dotted notation, and can convert them all to a common format:

```r
txt <- "eth0 00:00:5e:00:53:2a, wlan0 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E, switch 001a.2b3c.4d5f"

search_MAC(txt)
#> [1] "00:00:5E:00:53:2A" "00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E" "001A.2B3C.4D5F"

search_MAC(txt, normalize = TRUE)
#> [1] "00:00:5E:00:53:2A" "00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E" "00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5F"

is_MAC(c("00:00:5E:00:53:2A", "00:00:5E:00:53"))
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE

normalize_MAC("0000.5e00.532a", sep = "-")
#> [1] "00-00-5E-00-53-2A"
```

### Who made this device?

`lookup_vendor()` identifies the manufacturer using the IEEE **MA-L** (the
classic 24-bit OUI), **MA-M** (28-bit) and **MA-S** (36-bit) registries. They
are downloaded once by `get_oui_registry()` and cached with
`tools::R_user_dir()`, so later lookups work offline:

```r
lookup_vendor(get_MAC())
#> [1] "ASUSTek COMPUTER INC." "Intel Corporate"
```

### Address bits and conversions

Two bits of the first byte carry meaning. The **multicast** bit marks group
addresses, and the **locally administered** bit marks addresses that were not
assigned by the IEEE, such as the randomized addresses of phones or the ones of
virtual machines, so they will not have a vendor:

```r
is_local_MAC("DA:A1:19:00:00:00")
#> [1] TRUE

is_multicast_MAC("01:00:5E:00:00:FB")
#> [1] TRUE

# Random locally administered addresses, e.g. for virtual machines
set.seed(1)
random_MAC(2)
#> [1] "FA:80:D6:D1:E0:69" "42:A1:2A:BA:54:B5"
```

`eui64_MAC()` derives the IPv6 interface identifier (modified EUI-64,
[RFC 4291](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291#appendix-A)) and the
link-local address of an interface:

```r
eui64_MAC("00:00:5E:00:53:2A", link_local = TRUE)
#> [1] "fe80::200:5eff:fe00:532a"
```

---

## Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `get_MAC()` | MAC addresses of the local network interfaces |
| `get_arp_table()` | IP and MAC addresses of the neighbors in the ARP cache |
| `search_MAC()` | Extract MAC addresses from text |
| `is_MAC()` | Check whether strings are valid MAC addresses |
| `normalize_MAC()` | Convert to a common notation (`XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX` by default) |
| `is_local_MAC()` | Check the locally administered bit |
| `is_multicast_MAC()` | Check the multicast (group) bit |
| `random_MAC()` | Generate random (by default locally administered) addresses |
| `eui64_MAC()` | IPv6 modified EUI-64 identifier and link-local address |
| `get_oui_registry()` | Download (and cache) the IEEE MA-L, MA-M and MA-S registries |
| `lookup_vendor()` | Organization that owns each MAC address block |
